mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.0% per annum signals a tightening monetary policy regime that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.0%, or the average 20-day return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% indicates a tight labor market that pressures firms to raise wages, increasing input costs and reducing profit margins, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 3.5%, or the mean return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction permits above 1.4 million units per month signals strong household demand for housing, which correlates with rising consumer confidence and higher consumption, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1.4 million, or the average 60-day return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production below 104.0 (2017=100) indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate output and signals deteriorating economic momentum, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 104.0, or the average 5-day return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS signal a persistent inflationary environment that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where both CPIAUCSL > 295.0 and FEDFUNDS > 2.0%, or the joint signal fails to produce a statistically significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PAYEMS and decline in UNRATE indicates strong labor market momentum that increases wage pressures and corporate labor costs, reducing earnings visibility and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 100k in 1 month AND UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS rises >100k and UNRATE falls >0.2pp, or the joint signal does not produce a statistically significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above 680 billion dollars, combined with rising housing starts (HOUST), signals strong aggregate demand that supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS > 680.0 and HOUST > 1400.0, or the joint signal fails to produce a statistically significant positive return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production below 104.0 and a concurrent drop in GDP growth (GDPC1) below 1.5% annualized signals a weakening supply chain and deteriorating economic momentum, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO < 104.0 and GDPC1 < 1.5%, or the joint signal fails to produce a statistically significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).
